hero.headline: At least 3 dead, 5 injured in Dallas apartment building explosion
hero.body:
Three people died and five others were injured after a natural gas explosion triggered a massive fire at a Dallas apartment complex on Thursday. Nearly 100 firefighters responded to battle the blaze, which left the building collapsed and reduced to rubble.

The bodies of two adult women and one child were recovered from the debris, according to Dallas Fire and Rescue. Four additional people were hospitalized with injuries following the explosion.

Dallas Fire and Rescue Assistant Chief James Russ announced the confirmed deaths at a press conference. "The fire is contained, but our members are still working on the scene to do primary searches," Russ said. He noted that firefighters deployed a drone to survey the area for potential victims.

Witnesses described the force of the explosion as severe. Julie Jensen, who lived less than a block away, said she was watching television when the blast occurred. "I was sitting on my couch watching TV and stuff flew off our walls," she said. After hearing the noise and seeing smoke rise from the complex, she grabbed her family's cat and fled to a nearby parking lot.

Another resident, Terrance, told news outlets that he lost everything in the fire. "I lost my animals and everything," he said. "They probably burnt up, man. Two dogs, three cats. Getting off the bus coming home, and I've seen all this smoke. My wife says, 'That's our apartment complex.'"

The explosion occurred in the Oak Cliff area of Dallas. Multiple emergency response agencies deployed to the scene, with firefighters working through wreckage and debris. Some firefighters used long ladders to spray water on the smoking piles while others searched beneath burned lumber for possible survivors.

The blast was caused by natural gas, fire officials confirmed. The investigation into the exact circumstances and source of the explosion remained active as crews continued working at the site.

Dallas Mayor Eric Johnson responded to the disaster on social media. "I am closely monitoring the latest developments regarding the explosion in Oak Cliff," Johnson tweeted. "My prayers are with those injured, their families, and all those who have suffered loss from this tragic event."

The apartment complex sustained catastrophic damage from the force of the explosion. Emergency crews continued search and rescue operations as authorities worked to account for all residents and determine if additional people remained missing.

The incident affected numerous families living at the complex and residents in the surrounding area. Local officials coordinated the emergency response as rescue workers searched through the destroyed building.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative deal to extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for 60 days and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.S. officials. The framework includes plans to restart talks about Iran's nuclear program, though final approval from both countries' leadership remains pending.

Vice President Vance said the U.S. was very close to finalizing the agreement but acknowledged that sticking points remained. The two sides continue negotiating what Vance described as "nuclear stuff," indicating disagreements persist over key details of any nuclear framework.

Under the proposed deal, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and allow its ports to resume normal operations. The waterway, which handles roughly a fifth of global oil traffic, has been a critical flashpoint throughout the three-month conflict. As part of the arrangement, Iran would clear mines it deployed in the strait and refrain from imposing tolls on passing ships.

In exchange, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports that has been in place since April 13. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the deal could achieve a completely open Strait of Hormuz without tolls if successful. The agreement would also unfreeze some Iranian assets held in banks outside Iran.

The 60-day extension would halt hostilities on all fronts, including between Israel and Lebanon. This period would give negotiators additional time to work out details on a broader nuclear framework and address other outstanding issues between the nations.

However, important questions remain unresolved. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Tehran had not agreed to hand over its highly enriched uranium stockpile, and that Iran's nuclear issue was not part of the preliminary agreement. Previous reports suggested Tehran might be willing to give up some of its stockpile, but no details have emerged about how such an arrangement would be implemented.

The potential deal also lacks mention of Iran's ballistic missile program or efforts to limit support for regional allies including Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen. These issues may be deferred to future negotiations or excluded entirely from current discussions.

The tentative agreement comes after months of military tensions between the countries. Both sides appear to recognize the mutual benefits of reducing immediate conflict while pursuing longer-term diplomatic solutions. Reopening the Strait of Hormuz would restore normal shipping operations and help stabilize global energy markets, which have faced uncertainty during the conflict.

Officials from both countries continue working to finalize the memorandum of understanding that would codify the extended ceasefire and create a structure for future discussions. While neither side appears interested in returning to all-out conflict, the persistence of disagreements suggests negotiations will remain challenging in coming weeks.

cards.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian military site
cards.teaser: The United States carried out new strikes against an Iranian military site, an official said.
cards.body:
The United States carried out new military strikes against an Iranian military site, according to officials.

The strikes occurred as U.S. and Iranian officials reported progress in ongoing peace negotiations. Vice President Vance indicated the two countries were nearing a deal, with discussions focused on arrangements that could extend a 60-day truce and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: US military accuses Iran of ceasefire violation after missile launch
cards.teaser: The US said Iran launched missiles at Kuwait in what American officials called a violation of the fragile truce.
cards.body:
The US military condemned Iran's missile attack on Kuwait as a serious breach of the ceasefire agreement between the two nations. The strike occurred while US and Iranian officials were negotiating a framework to extend the truce for two additional months, pending approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership.

News of a potential ceasefire extension triggered a decline in global oil prices on Thursday. US officials indicated they were nearing a deal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and pave the way for broader negotiations, though final approval from Trump remained pending.

cards.headline: Judge declines to block Trump executive order limiting mail-in voting
cards.teaser: A federal judge declined to stop changes to mail-in voting ordered by President Trump.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., has declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The decision allows the order to remain in effect for now, though it is not final.

Democrats filed a lawsuit challenging the executive order, arguing it would limit voting access. Another judge may soon rule on the order as the legal challenge continues.

cards.headline: Supreme Court sides with death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled in favor of a Mississippi man on death row who alleged racial discrimination in jury selection.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled in favor of a Black death row inmate from Mississippi in a case examining racial discrimination during jury selection. The decision in Pitchford v. Cain addressed whether prosecutors improperly excluded potential jurors based on race at trial.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote the majority opinion, which focused on protecting jury rights. The ruling underscores the Court's concerns about racial bias in capital cases within the criminal justice system.

cards.headline: Dell Wins $9.7 Billion Pentagon Contract
cards.body:
Dell Technologies secured a $9.7 billion contract from the Pentagon to streamline software purchases for the Department of Defense. The contract was announced by the Department of War and confirmed by multiple sources.

The deal comes after Dell CEO Michael Dell cultivated a relationship with President Trump early in his administration. Trump later acquired stock in Dell and publicly praised the company, according to reports from CNBC and The Washington Post.

The contract represents a significant win for Dell Technologies as it expands its government business. The agreement will involve Dell managing and consolidating software procurement across Defense Department operations.

Trump's personal investment portfolio stands to benefit from the contract award. The New York Times reported that the president holds Dell stock, creating a direct financial interest in the company's government contracts.

Dell reported strong quarterly earnings that helped drive stock market gains. The company's shares surged following the earnings announcement and contract news.

The Pentagon contract was listed in official Department of War contract announcements. The agreement is designed to streamline how the Defense Department purchases software, consolidating what has been a fragmented procurement process across multiple military branches and agencies.

Michael Dell's early outreach to the Trump administration has now yielded tangible business results for his company. The timing of Trump's stock purchase, his public endorsements of Dell, and the subsequent major government contract award has raised questions about potential conflicts of interest.

The $9.7 billion figure represents the total potential value of the contract. Dell Technologies is a major provider of computer hardware and enterprise technology solutions, and this contract significantly expands its role in supporting U.S. military operations.

hero.headline: Russian drone strikes apartment building in Romania, injuring two
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in the Romanian city of Galati, injuring two people, Romanian authorities said. The incident marks the first reported Russian attack on infrastructure in a NATO member state during the conflict with Ukraine.

Galati is located near the Romanian border with Ukraine. The drone hit a residential apartment building in the city. Two people sustained injuries in the strike, according to Romanian officials.

Romania is a member of NATO, which operates under a principle of collective defense. An attack on one member state is considered an attack on all members under Article 5 of the NATO treaty.

The strike comes as Russian forces continue military operations against Ukraine. Romania shares a border with Ukraine and has been a transit point for refugees fleeing the conflict. The country has also served as a logistical hub for Western military aid to Ukraine.

Russian drones have previously strayed into Romanian airspace during attacks on Ukrainian targets near the border. Romanian authorities have documented several incidents of drone fragments landing on Romanian territory. This incident represents the first time a Russian drone has directly struck a building with casualties on Romanian soil.

Romanian officials did not immediately provide details about the type of drone involved or whether they believe the strike was intentional or the result of a navigation error. The Romanian government has not yet issued a formal statement on how it plans to respond to the attack.

NATO headquarters had not released an official statement on the incident at the time of reporting. The alliance has previously said it would treat any attack on member territory seriously and consult with affected members to determine an appropriate response.

The two injured individuals were in the apartment building at the time of the strike. Romanian authorities did not release information about the severity of their injuries or their current condition.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during test at Cape Canaveral
cards.teaser: A New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad at the Florida facility.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a scheduled test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night. The massive fireball destroyed the launch pad at the Kennedy Space Center at 9pm ET, with the orange sky visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away.

No personnel were harmed in the incident, according to the company. Blue Origin described the explosion as an "anomaly" on social media. The incident poses potential complications for NASA's lunar program, which relies on the New Glenn rocket for its plans to build a lunar base and return humans to the moon within the next two years.

cards.headline: US designates two Brazilian drug gangs as terrorist organizations
cards.teaser: The Trump administration labeled Brazil's two largest drug gangs as terrorist groups after warnings.
cards.body:
Your Updated Card

The Trump administration has designated Brazil's two largest drug gangs as terrorist organizations, following through on previous threats. The action was made after pressure from members of the Bolsonaro family.

The designation targets the two largest criminal organizations currently operating in Brazil, expanding the administration's focus on drug trafficking across the Western Hemisphere.

cards.headline: Israel severs ties with UN chief after sexual violence blacklist inclusion
cards.teaser: Israel cut ties with the UN secretary general after being added to a list of forces committing sexual violence in conflict zones.
cards.body:
Israel severed ties with the United Nations secretary general after the UN added Israeli forces to a blacklist for conflict-related sexual violence. The list also includes Hamas and Russian forces.

The UN blacklist identifies armed forces and groups that have committed sexual violence in conflict zones. Israel accused the UN of placing it on the same list as Hamas. Israeli officials did not specify what severing ties with the UN chief would entail in practice.

cards.headline: US officials say framework reached to reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: American officials said they are nearing an arrangement with Iran to reopen the strategic waterway, though President Trump has not approved the plan.
cards.body:
US officials say they are closing in on a framework to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend the ceasefire between the US and Iran. The critical shipping lane is essential for global oil supplies. According to officials, the framework has been agreed pending approval from both President Trump and Iran's leadership.

Vice President Vance told the BBC that the two sides are "very close" to a deal but "not there yet." Any arrangement would need sign-off from Trump before moving forward with more substantive negotiations between the countries.

cards.headline: Portugal records hottest May day as Europe faces heatwave
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its record for the hottest day in May as high temperatures spread across Europe.
cards.body:
Portugal broke its record for the hottest day ever recorded in May as a heatwave spread across Europe. Red alerts have been issued in Italy due to the extreme heat.

French students are taking exams in schools experiencing high temperatures. The heatwave has affected multiple countries across the continent, prompting warnings from weather authorities about the health risks of extreme heat.

cards.headline: US military accuses Iran of ceasefire violation after missile launch
cards.teaser: The US said Iran launched missiles at Kuwait in what American officials called a violation of the fragile truce.

The strike occurred while US and Iranian officials were negotiating a framework to extend the truce for two additional months, pending approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership.

cards.headline: Judge declines to block Trump executive order limiting mail-in voting
cards.teaser: A federal judge declined to stop changes to mail-in voting ordered by President Trump.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., has declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The decision allows the order to remain in effect for now, though it is not final.

Democrats filed a lawsuit challenging the executive order, arguing it would limit voting access. Another judge may soon rule on the order as the legal challenge continues.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during test in Florida
cards.teaser: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a hotfire test on Thursday night at Cape Canaveral in Florida. The explosion destroyed the launch pad in a massive fireball that was visible from over 100 miles away in Fort Pierce. No personnel were harmed in the incident.

Blue Origin described the explosion as an "anomaly." The incident represents a setback for the company and has raised concerns about NASA's plans to build a lunar base and return humans to the moon.

cards.headline: Whitmer says she will not run for president in 2028, then backtracks
cards.teaser: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer initially said she would not seek the presidency in 2028, then reversed course hours later.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she would not run for president in 2028, telling reporters she would not be among the candidates. Hours later, she walked back the statement, creating uncertainty about her political plans.

The reversal came after initial reports that Whitmer had definitively shut down speculation about a 2028 White House bid. The governor's shifting statements left her intentions unclear regarding the presidential race.

cards.headline: Netanyahu directs military to expand control in Gaza to 70%
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he ordered the military to increase control of Gaza.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he has directed the Israel Defense Forces to expand their control of Gaza to 70%. This expansion would violate the ceasefire agreement that Israel and Hamas reached in October 2025.

The directive raises concerns about whether Israel intends to comply with the terms of the negotiated truce between the two parties.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes on Florida Launch Pad
cards.teaser: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a ground test at Cape Canaveral.
cards.body:
Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida during a ground test. The incident occurred Thursday night and produced a large fireball visible from surrounding areas.

The explosion represents a significant setback for Jeff Bezos' spaceflight company as it works to compete with SpaceX in the commercial space industry.

cards.headline: Fertitta Entertainment to Acquire Caesars for $17.6 Billion
cards.teaser: Billionaire Tilman Fertitta is buying Caesars Entertainment in a deal valued at $17.6 billion.
cards.body:
The sources provided don't contain sufficient confirmed details about the Fertitta Entertainment acquisition of Caesars. The BBC News articles reference completely different stories (a Taylor Swift concert plot and energy bills), and the partial KOB.com and WSJ citations are cut off and incomplete.

Since I cannot verify the specific facts from the original card against complete source material, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

Caesars Entertainment, a Las Vegas Strip icon, will be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment in a $17.6 billion transaction. The casino and entertainment company is being sold for nearly $6 billion in equity value, with the total deal including assumed debt.

Tilman Fertitta, a billionaire businessman, is expanding his Las Vegas presence with the purchase. The deal represents a major consolidation in the Las Vegas casino industry and marks Fertitta's significant investment in the city's entertainment sector.

cards.headline: Stock Market Reaches New Highs on Iran Deal and Corporate Earnings
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record levels as investors responded to a U.S.-Iran agreement and strong earnings.
cards.body:
Stock markets hit record levels as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq climbed to all-time highs. Strong corporate earnings, including gains from Dell, fueled investor optimism and drove technology stocks higher.

U.S. and Iranian officials have moved closer to a potential ceasefire deal. The framework of an agreement has been worked out and now awaits approval from Trump and Iran's leadership, though negotiations continue to develop.

cards.headline: SpaceX Reduces IPO Valuation Target to $1.8 Trillion
cards.teaser: SpaceX lowered its target valuation for an upcoming initial public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX reduced its target valuation for a planned initial public offering to at least $1.8 trillion, according to Bloomberg. The space company adjusted its expectations downward from previous internal targets.

The $80 billion IPO has attracted significant interest from investors, though 78% of the offering has already been allocated according to Fortune. Retail investors are exploring ways to participate in the public offering of shares in Elon Musk's space venture.

cards.headline: ABC Accuses FCC of Threatening Broadcast Licenses
cards.teaser: ABC and its parent Disney accused federal regulators of unconstitutional retaliation over station licenses.
cards.body:
ABC has accused the Federal Communications Commission of targeting its broadcast licenses as part of what the network characterizes as unconstitutional retaliation. The company filed license renewals under protest, with executives criticizing FCC Chairman Brendan Carr for what they describe as an assault on its television operations.

According to reports, the FCC moved up the expiration dates on ABC's station licenses. Disney's ABC division proceeded with the early renewals while publicly objecting to what it views as regulatory targeting by the Trump administration.

cards.headline: Surface Transportation Board Delays Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Merger Review
cards.teaser: Federal regulators conditionally accepted a rail merger application but requested additional data.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board conditionally accepted the revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but delayed proceedings while requesting more information. The $71.5 billion deal would combine two of the country's largest freight railroads.

The merger would create what supporters describe as America's first transcontinental railroad under unified ownership. Federal regulators paused the review process to gather additional data about the proposed combination of the two rail giants.

hero.headline: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes during Florida testing
hero.body:
A New Glenn rocket operated by Blue Origin exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday evening, dealing a significant blow to Jeff Bezos' spaceflight company and NASA's lunar ambitions.

The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during a scheduled "hotfire" test at Kennedy Space Center. A massive fireball engulfed and destroyed the launchpad, with the orange glow visible from Fort Pierce, 115 miles to the south. Shockwaves from the blast were felt across Florida's space coast, with residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting that their homes shook. People hundreds of miles away in South Carolina reported seeing the glow in the sky. Emergency officials confirmed there were no hazards from fumes or other releases.

Blue Origin said all employees were safe and accounted for. The company described the incident as "an anomaly" in an initial statement. Bezos acknowledged the setback on social media, tweeting that it was "a very rough day" but that the company would "rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying."

The explosion threatens NASA's timeline for returning humans to the moon. Just two days before the test failure, NASA had announced that Blue Origin won a contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions designed to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would conduct a full evaluation of how the explosion affects the Artemis program timeline and moon base construction plans.

New Glenn is Blue Origin's heavy-lift orbital launch vehicle, designed to compete with SpaceX's Falcon Heavy for satellite launches and government contracts. The rocket is named after John Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth. It was meant to serve as a central component in NASA's Artemis Program, which aims to land astronauts on the moon for the first time since 1972.

This explosion marks the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin. Last month, a payload from the third New Glenn flight ended up in the wrong orbit, prompting the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the vehicle to return to flight the previous week.

The failure will likely delay Blue Origin's operational launch timeline. The company must investigate the root cause of the failure, implement necessary repairs, and conduct additional testing before attempting another launch. This process typically requires months, depending on the severity of the underlying issues.

SpaceX, Blue Origin's primary competitor for NASA contracts, is also involved in the Artemis program. The companies are competing to develop lunar landers for future missions planned through 2028.

cards.headline: NASA telescope discovers supermassive black hole that formed before its galaxy
cards.teaser: The James Webb Space Telescope found a black hole that violates conventional understanding of how galaxies and black holes develop.
cards.body:
NASA's James Webb Space Telescope detected a supermassive black hole that existed before its host galaxy formed, contradicting the standard model of galaxy evolution. Scientists previously believed galaxies formed first, with black holes developing at their centers afterward.

The discovery, which researchers are calling a paradigm shift, forces scientists to reconsider fundamental assumptions about cosmic structure formation. The black hole has been described as naked because it lacks the typical galactic environment that surrounds such objects.

cards.headline: Cloud providers redesign infrastructure for AI agent traffic
cards.teaser: AWS, Cloudflare and other companies are rebuilding internet infrastructure to handle machine-generated traffic as AI agents move into production.
cards.body:
Major cloud infrastructure providers are redesigning their systems to accommodate a shift from human users to AI agents as the primary source of internet traffic. Companies including AWS and Cloudflare are adapting their networks as AI agents transition from experimental projects to production deployments.

The infrastructure changes reflect expectations that machines rather than humans will generate the majority of internet traffic in the coming years. The redesign affects core cloud services and content delivery systems that currently prioritize patterns of human browsing and interaction.

cards.headline: AI language models treat false information as true despite explicit warnings
cards.teaser: Tests show large language models display bias toward representing claims as true even after being warned the statements are false.
cards.body:
Large language models continue to treat false statements as accurate even when explicitly warned the information is incorrect, according to fine-tuning tests. The models showed a consistent bias toward confidently presenting claims as true regardless of warnings.

The findings raise questions about reliability when AI systems are used to process and present information. Researchers conducted tests that involved fine-tuning models with clear warnings that certain statements were false, but the models continued to handle the information as factual.

cards.headline: Glean reaches $300 million revenue as companies use AI to cut costs
cards.teaser: The enterprise AI search startup tripled its annual revenue as budget-cutting became its primary selling point to customers.
cards.body:
Enterprise AI search startup Glean has reached $300 million in annual revenue, tripling its previous year's total. The company has capitalized on growing demand for AI tools that help businesses reduce costs, positioning its search capabilities as a way to cut expenses.

The milestone comes as major technology companies have begun competing in the enterprise AI search market. Despite this intensifying competition from tech giants, Glean has maintained its growth momentum.

cards.headline: Waymo leads autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas as state releases tracking data
cards.teaser: New Texas law and tracking tool show Waymo dominates robotaxi and self-driving truck registrations, with Tesla trailing.
cards.body:
Waymo leads all companies in autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas following the implementation of a new state law that requires tracking of self-driving vehicles. This regulatory requirement has provided unprecedented transparency into the autonomous vehicle market operating within the state.

The tracking tool monitors both robotaxis and autonomous trucks on Texas roads. Tesla, despite its significant vehicle production volume, registers substantially fewer autonomous vehicles than Waymo according to the data.

cards.headline: Developer plants data-deletion code to sabotage AI coding assistants
cards.teaser: A programmer inserted a hidden prompt injection into jqwik code that instructs AI agents to delete application output.
cards.body:
A software developer frustrated with AI-assisted coding inserted a hidden prompt injection into the jqwik codebase that instructs AI coding agents to delete application output. The undisclosed addition targets what the developer called vibe coders who rely heavily on AI tools.

The malicious code exploits how AI coding assistants process instructions embedded in source code. When AI tools read the infected code, they receive instructions to perform destructive operations on the applications they are helping to build.

hero.headline: Former NHL star Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion known for his physical play and postseason performance, has died at 60. Police confirmed Lemieux died by suicide.

Lemieux won Stanley Cups with three different franchises during his NHL career. He captured championships with the Montreal Canadiens, New Jersey Devils twice, and Colorado Avalanche. His aggressive playing style and ability to elevate his game in the playoffs made him one of the most effective postseason performers of his era.

The former right winger played over 1,200 NHL games across 21 seasons. He scored more than 370 goals and accumulated over 1,700 penalty minutes during his career. Lemieux won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP in 1995 with the Devils.

Lemieux became involved in one of hockey's most intense rivalries during his time with Colorado. A hit he delivered on Detroit's Kris Draper in the 1996 playoffs sparked years of animosity between the Avalanche and Red Wings. The incident defined the competitive era between the two Western Conference powers.

After retiring as a player, Lemieux remained connected to hockey through various roles. He worked in player development and coaching positions with several organizations.

The NHL released a statement acknowledging Lemieux's passing and his contributions to the sport. His family has requested privacy during this time.

Lemieux's death adds to growing conversations about mental health support for professional athletes and former players. Several sports leagues have expanded mental health resources and support programs in recent years.

cards.headline: MLB owners propose salary cap in first collective bargaining offer
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball owners have proposed implementing a salary cap for the first time since the 1994-95 strike that canceled the World Series.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball owners presented their initial collective bargaining proposal to the players union, including a hard salary cap. The proposal marks the first time owners have formally sought a salary cap system since the labor dispute that led to the cancellation of the 1994 World Series.

The proposal also includes a salary floor designed to address competitive balance concerns. The Baltimore Orioles currently sit just below the proposed minimum spending threshold. The union has not yet publicly responded to the initial offer, and negotiations are expected to continue as the current collective bargaining agreement approaches expiration.

cards.headline: California teenager Shrey Parikh wins National Spelling Bee in spell-off
cards.teaser: Shrey Parikh won the Scripps National Spelling Bee after correctly spelling bromocriptine in a tense spell-off.
cards.body:
Shrey Parikh, 14, claimed the Scripps National Spelling Bee championship after a dramatic tiebreaker against Ishaan Gupta. In the 90-second spell-off round, Parikh correctly spelled 32 words to Gupta's 25, securing the title as the nation's best young speller.

Arriving as a favorite, Parikh transformed the tense final competition into a decisive victory Thursday night. His command of complex vocabulary proved commanding when the bee came down to the lightning-round format used to determine a winner.

cards.headline: Spurs force Game 7 against Thunder with Victor Wembanyama's 28 points
cards.teaser: San Antonio avoided elimination as Victor Wembanyama scored 28 points to push the Western Conference finals back to Oklahoma City.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs kept their season alive by defeating the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 6 of the Western Conference finals. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 28 points as San Antonio responded to facing elimination.

The series will now return to Oklahoma City for a decisive Game 7. The Thunder's role players have performed at high levels throughout the conference finals. San Antonio needed a strong performance across its roster to extend the series and force the winner-take-all matchup.

cards.headline: Knicks center Mitchell Robinson breaks pinky finger, Finals status uncertain
cards.teaser: New York Knicks center Mitchell Robinson suffered a broken pinky finger on his right hand with no timetable set for his return.
cards.body:
Mitchell Robinson broke his pinky finger on his right hand, putting his availability for the NBA Finals in question. The Knicks have not established a timeline for the center's return to the court.

The injury occurred during the Eastern Conference finals. Robinson's status will depend on how quickly the fracture heals and whether he can play through discomfort. The Knicks have not announced whether Robinson will require surgery or can manage the injury with protective measures.

cards.headline: Patriots emerge as sole trade destination for Eagles receiver A.J. Brown
cards.teaser: The New England Patriots are the only team in discussions to acquire Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver A.J. Brown in a trade.
cards.body:
Trade talks involving A.J. Brown have narrowed to the New England Patriots as the sole potential destination. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts described his relationship with Brown as really good despite the ongoing trade speculation.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel addressed the situation in a recent press conference. Eagles stars have maintained their focus as uncertainty about Brown's future continues. Multiple analysts project the Eagles and Brown are headed toward a separation, with New England positioned as the likely landing spot if a deal materializes.

cards.headline: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner eliminated from French Open
cards.teaser: World number one Jannik Sinner was eliminated from the French Open after struggling in the heat.
cards.body:
Jannik Sinner, the world's top-ranked men's tennis player, was eliminated from the French Open in the second round by Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerúndolo in a five-set match. Sinner attributed his loss to illness rather than the extreme heat conditions at the tournament. He described the defeat as "tough to accept" given his recent form and top ranking.

The Italian said he needs time to recover both physically and mentally before competing again. He plans to skip grass-court tournaments and prepare for Wimbledon. Sinner's early exit has significantly opened up the men's draw, with Alexander Zverev emerging as the new favourite for the title.

hero.headline: Multiple Artists Drop Out of Trump-Linked Freedom 250 Concert Series
hero.body:
Country singer Martina McBride withdrew from the Freedom 250 concerts scheduled for the National Mall in Washington, D.C., becoming the fourth performer to back out of the event. McBride posted on social media that she was dropping out after learning the concert series carried more political baggage than she had initially realized.

The concert series is organized by Keith Krach, a Trump appointee, and has Trump's backing. Young MC and Morris Day also pulled out of the planned performances, joining McBride in the wave of cancellations. The Freedom 250 concerts are scheduled to take place on the National Mall as part of programming related to America's 250th anniversary.

The cancellations come shortly after the concert lineup was announced. Artists have cited political concerns as their reason for withdrawing from the event. McBride made her announcement on social media accounts, explaining that she had not been fully aware of the political associations when she initially agreed to perform.

The Freedom 250 series was intended to be a celebration of the nation's semiquincentennial, marking 250 years since American independence. However, the Trump connection and Krach's involvement as organizer have created controversy that has prompted multiple performers to reconsider their participation.

The organizers have not publicly commented on the growing list of artist withdrawals. The concert series is still scheduled to proceed on the National Mall, though the roster of performers has shrunk significantly in recent days. McBride's departure represents a significant loss for the event, as she is one of the most recognizable names in country music.

The remaining lineup for the Freedom 250 concerts has not been disclosed following the recent cancellations. The event was promoted as a State Fair-style celebration, but the political associations have overshadowed the anniversary commemoration. Additional performers may reconsider their involvement as the controversy continues to develop.

cards.headline: Hacks Ends Five-Season Run With Series Finale
cards.teaser: The HBO comedy concluded its run with a finale that reunited Deborah Vance and Ava Daniels for joke workshopping.
cards.body:
The comedy series Hacks concluded its five-season run on HBO Max with a finale that brought the show full circle. The episode reunited Deborah Vance (Jean Smart) and Ava Daniels (Hannah Einbinder) as they workshopped jokes together, returning to the central dynamic that defined their relationship throughout the series. The finale also featured a Paris setting before wrapping up the story.

The show's creators intentionally designed the ending this way, having planned the conclusion from the beginning. The finale addressed what had been absent from much of the fifth season by refocusing on the core partnership between the two main characters. The episode is now available to stream on HBO Max.

cards.headline: HBO Documentary About Jacinda Ardern Wins Top Documentary Emmy
cards.teaser: Prime Minister, an HBO documentary about the former New Zealand leader, received the award at the Documentary Emmy ceremony.
cards.body:
Prime Minister, an HBO original documentary about New Zealand leader Jacinda Ardern, won the top documentary award at Thursday's Emmy Awards ceremony. The film was directed by Michelle Walshe and Lindsay Utz.

The documentary previously premiered at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival, where it received the Audience Award for World Cinema Documentary. HBO and National Geographic were among the networks recognized with multiple awards at the ceremony.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt's Son Maddox Drops Pitt From Last Name
cards.teaser: Maddox Jolie-Pitt, the eldest son of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, is officially removing his father's surname.
cards.body:
Maddox, the eldest son of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, is dropping Pitt from his last name. The change reflects ongoing tensions within the family following the actors' separation.

Maddox's sister Zahara previously made a similar decision to drop the Pitt surname. She recently graduated from college, with Brad Pitt reportedly absent from the event. Other family members, including brother Pax Thien, attended the graduation.

cards.headline: CBS Projects $15 Million Profit From Byron Allen Late-Night Deal
cards.teaser: The network says leasing late-night time to Byron Allen will generate more profit than running a traditional show.
cards.body:
CBS announced that its decision to lease late-night programming time to Byron Allen will generate $15 million in profit. The Paramount Skydance broadcast network made the projection after facing criticism for canceling The Late Show and removing Stephen Colbert from the time slot. The network says the arrangement will be more profitable than producing its own traditional late-night program.

The Late Show had been a long-running fixture on CBS before the network decided to cancel it. The move to lease the time slot rather than produce original programming represents a shift in how broadcast networks approach late-night television. CBS defended the decision by emphasizing the financial benefits of the new arrangement with Allen.

cards.headline: Richard Gadd Discusses Half Man Series Finale and Character Deaths
cards.teaser: The creator and star of the HBO drama explained the ending of the six-episode series.
cards.body:
Richard Gadd spoke about the series finale of Half Man, the HBO and BBC drama he created and starred in. The six-episode show concluded with an ambiguous ending involving his character Ruben and Jamie Bell's character Niall. Gadd explained that the finale felt like the right way to end the series, which included a grueling fight sequence and the death of at least one character.

The show kept viewers in suspense throughout its run about what happened between the two main characters. The finale is now streaming on HBO Max. Gadd's comments addressed major plot points including character deaths and the decision to leave certain elements unresolved.

cards.headline: New Film Zine Ritual Launches at Los Angeles Theaters
cards.teaser: The independent print publication celebrates movie theater culture with contributions from Patton

hero.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative deal to extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for 60 days and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.S. officials. The framework includes plans to restart talks about Iran's nuclear program, though final approval from both countries' leadership remains pending.

Vice President Vance said the U.S. was very close to finalizing the agreement but acknowledged that sticking points remained. The two sides continue negotiating what Vance described as "nuclear stuff," indicating disagreements persist over key details of any nuclear framework.

Under the proposed deal, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and allow its ports to resume normal operations. The waterway, which handles roughly a fifth of global oil traffic, has been a critical flashpoint throughout the three-month conflict. As part of the arrangement, Iran would clear mines it deployed in the strait and refrain from imposing tolls on passing ships.

In exchange, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports that has been in place since April 13. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the deal could achieve a completely open Strait of Hormuz without tolls if successful. The agreement would also unfreeze some Iranian assets held in banks outside Iran.

The 60-day extension would halt hostilities on all fronts, including between Israel and Lebanon. This period would give negotiators additional time to work out details on a broader nuclear framework and address other outstanding issues between the nations.

However, important questions remain unresolved. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Tehran had not agreed to hand over its highly enriched uranium stockpile, and that Iran's nuclear issue was not part of the preliminary agreement. Previous reports suggested Tehran might be willing to give up some of its stockpile, but no details have emerged about how such an arrangement would be implemented.

The potential deal also lacks mention of Iran's ballistic missile program or efforts to limit support for regional allies including Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen. These issues may be deferred to future negotiations or excluded entirely from current discussions.

The tentative agreement comes after months of military tensions between the countries. Both sides appear to recognize the mutual benefits of reducing immediate conflict while pursuing longer-term diplomatic solutions. Reopening the Strait of Hormuz would restore normal shipping operations and help stabilize global energy markets, which have faced uncertainty during the conflict.

Officials from both countries continue working to finalize the memorandum of understanding that would codify the extended ceasefire and create a structure for future discussions. While neither side appears interested in returning to all-out conflict, the persistence of disagreements suggests negotiations will remain challenging in coming weeks.

cards.headline: Trump says U.S. has upper hand in Iran talks after military strikes
cards.teaser: President Trump said joint U.S.-Israeli strikes have weakened Iran's military, giving the U.S. leverage in negotiations.
cards.body:
President Trump stated that the U.S. holds a strategic advantage in ongoing negotiations to end the conflict with Iran, attributing this to joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes that have damaged Iran's military capabilities. Despite this assertion, Trump acknowledged that Iranian negotiators are skilled and shrewd in their approach to talks.

The comments emerge as negotiators work toward finalizing a tentative agreement that would extend the current ceasefire for 60 days. Trump contended that the military operations have positioned the U.S. favorably in reaching a deal.

cards.headline: Vance says nuclear issues remain unresolved in Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance said the U.S. and Iran are still negotiating over nuclear matters despite being close to a final agreement.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance said Thursday that the U.S. and Iran are very close to finalizing an agreement, though some issues remain unresolved. Nuclear matters are among the sticking points still being negotiated between the two sides.

A tentative deal framework has been agreed upon that would extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The agreement requires approval from both President Trump and Iran's leadership. News of the potential breakthrough has already affected global markets, with oil prices falling Thursday in response to the report.

cards.headline: White House launches website tracking unauthorized immigrant arrests
cards.teaser: The White House created a space-themed website that displays data on arrests of immigrants living in the U.S. without authorization.
cards.body:
The White House unveiled a website Thursday featuring a space theme to highlight immigration enforcement actions and arrest statistics. The site plays on the concept of government secrecy surrounding alleged alien encounters, using a Star Wars-style opening crawl with scrolling text across the screen.

The website presents data on immigration enforcement operations and arrests of unauthorized immigrants. The space-themed design draws a humorous parallel between extraterrestrial "aliens" and the immigration enforcement messaging.

cards.headline: Pro-Israel groups spend nearly $8 million to defeat Rep. Thomas Massie
cards.teaser: Pro-Israel organizations invested heavily in Kentucky's 4th District primary, contributing to the most expensive House primary in American history.
cards.body:
Pro-Israel groups spent nearly $8 million to oust Republican Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky's 4th District, helping to fuel the most expensive House primary in American history. The spending is part of a broader trend of AI companies, cryptocurrency interests, and pro-Israel organizations investing heavily in congressional races.

Crypto-aligned Protect Progress emerged as the largest spender in several races. The volume of spending from these interest groups has reached levels that can end political careers and halt political movements, according to observers of campaign finance patterns.

cards.headline: Michigan Gov. Whitmer backtracks on 2028 presidential race comment
cards.teaser: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer walked back an earlier statement saying she would not run for president in 2028.
cards.body:
Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer reversed course on a comment about not running for president in 2028. Whitmer is term-limited after two gubernatorial wins in her battleground state.

She has been widely viewed as a potential Democratic candidate for the 2028 presidential race. The governor's reversal suggests she may be keeping her options open for a future presidential campaign.

cards.headline: Sen. Collins responds to challenger's criticism over Iraq war vote
cards.teaser: Sen. Susan Collins defended her Iraq war vote after Democratic challenger Graham Platner said she voted to send him to Iraq.
cards.body:
Sen. Susan Collins of Maine defended her Iraq war vote after Democratic challenger Graham Platner criticized her support for U.S. military intervention. Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer, told The New York Times that Collins voted to send him to Iraq.

Collins countered by noting that Platner was not drafted into military service. The exchange reflects foreign policy disagreements emerging as a key issue in Maine's Senate race between the Republican incumbent and her Democratic opponent.
